hints: Look at where each bridging O leaves the left-hand sugar and where it joins the right-hand sugar. Focus on carbon 1 (the anomeric carbon next to the ring O) and whether the bond points up or down.
Remember beta bonds point up from carbon 1 in the Haworth view, and then count to carbons 3 and 4 on the next N-acetylglucosamine and glucuronic acid units to get the numbers.
walkthrough:
**Spot the repeating monomers**

This is a mucopolysaccharide made of alternating units. One has $COOH$ on top (glucuronic acid) and the next has $CH_2OH$ on top plus $HN-C=O-CH_3$ below (N-acetylglucosamine). So we have two different glycosidic links alternating along the chain.

**Decide alpha or beta**

Look at carbon 1, the anomeric carbon joined to the ring O. In both types of link here, the bridging O leaves carbon 1 from the upper position. Up from carbon 1 means beta, not alpha. That already rules out options A and B.

**Count the carbon numbers 1,3 and 1,4**

Follow each bridge. One bridge goes from C1 of glucuronic acid to C3 of N-acetylglucosamine (the carbon bearing the $OH$ on the side). The next bridge goes from C1 of N-acetylglucosamine to C4 of the next glucuronic acid (the carbon bearing the $OH$ below the ring). So we have $\beta$-1,3 and $\beta$-1,4 links, which is option C.

options.A: Incorrect because both links leave carbon 1 from the beta (up) position, not the alpha (down) position.
options.B: Incorrect because the links are beta, not alpha, and there is no 1,6 link to a $CH_2OH$ carbon here.
options.C: Correct because the chain alternates a beta link from C1 to C3 and a beta link from C1 to C4, typical of hyaluronic acid.
options.D: Incorrect because although the bonds are beta, one is 1,3 not 1,6, and no branch to carbon 6 is shown.
